name: Non Odd
classification_notes: Abrupt, cropped terminals combined with high internal contrast push this away from a traditional soft-bracketed serif into something closer to an unconventional sans-serif hybrid, though the foundry classifies it as a serif.
summary: A serif with abrupt, cropped terminals and high internal contrast, deliberately breaking from soft traditional serif conventions.
description: Non Odd sets a rigid vertical structure against organic, high-contrast details, using cropped rather than bracketed terminals for a precise, slightly unsettled character. Three weights cover editorial and identity work without an italic. The foundry pitches it as sitting somewhere between sans and serif, built to avoid looking like anything else on the shelf.
foundry_blurb: Non Foundry describes Non Odd as exploring cropped terminals combined with high internal contrast, relying on abrupt cuts and assertive shapes rather than the softened strokes of traditional serifs, for editorial design and visual identity systems seeking a sophisticated yet unpretentious tone.

name: Non Ophélie Display
classification_notes: High contrast between thick and thin strokes, an expressive lowercase 'a' as its defining letter, and optimisation for large sizes place this firmly as a display face.
summary: A high-contrast display face built around an expressive, fluid lowercase 'a', now extended to Cyrillic and Greek.
description: Non Ophélie Display grew from a single letter, a fluid, fast-moving lowercase 'a', with that same energy carried through the rest of the alphabet. Six weights with italics perform best at large sizes, where the thin-thick contrast and terminal details read clearly. Version 2.0 added Cyrillic and Greek coverage plus stylistic ligatures and alternate capitals.
foundry_blurb: Non Foundry describes Non Ophélie Display as beginning with an expressive lowercase 'a' characterised by fluid curvature and a pronounced tail, with high contrast and terminal details making it a typeface that performs best at large sizes.

name: Non Pliant
classification_notes: A Swiss typographic structure built for functional, continuous text use across a wide range of environments places this as a general-purpose grotesque.
summary: A free, Swiss-structured grotesque built to cover text, display and typographic composition without losing legibility.
description: Non Pliant, formerly Non Bureau, started as an internal tool before being released as a free family for basic commercial use. Seven weights with italics cover continuous text reliably, and an Extended width variant broadens it for graphic applications. A dependable, no-cost workhorse rather than a display statement.
foundry_blurb: Non Foundry describes Non Pliant as having a Swiss typographic style structure that makes it a universal option, offered as a free download for basic commercial use, fulfilling core design functions across text, display and typographic compositions.

name: Non Sans
classification_notes: A dense, modular grotesque with clear roots in 1960s Swiss type design, refined in a 2022 revision, places this as a classic grotesque.
summary: A dense, modular grotesque rooted in 1960s Swiss type design, refined for editorial, interface and signage use.
description: Non Sans reads as compact and reliable, with a solid reading rhythm that traces back to the functional, modular shapes of 1960s Swiss type. A 2022 revision unified x-heights and weight consistency and added a slanted style alongside the existing rotation-based alternate. Five weights, each with slant and rotation variants, give it real range for identity, editorial and interface work.
foundry_blurb: Non Foundry describes Non Sans as a grotesque-style sans serif with a dense, robust and reliable appearance, its 2022 revised version refined for improved typographic performance with a more unified system of x-heights, width proportions and weight consistency.

name: Non Tempo
classification_notes: Inspired directly by Futura and Super Grotesk with subtle tension added to its curves, this is a contemporary geometric sans with a stencil companion.
summary: A contemporary geometric sans inspired by Futura and Super Grotesk, with subtle tension in its curves and a stencil companion.
description: Non Tempo takes the purity of classic geometric sans-serifs and introduces small tensions in its curves and diagonals rather than staying strictly rigid, adding texture to blocks of text. Ten weights from Thin to Heavy each have a stencil counterpart with small strategic cuts, doubling as a more experimental display option. A wide, deliberate range for a single geometric family.
foundry_blurb: Non Foundry describes Non Tempo as a geometric typeface inspired by modern classics such as Futura and Super Grotesk, introducing subtle tensions in its curves and diagonals for a contemporary reinterpretation of geometric sans serifs, complemented by a stencil version.
